newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Otter expects rise in gold output.
newsitem.headline: Otter expects rise in gold output.

text.p: New Zealand's Otter Gold Mines Ltd said on Wednesday it expected a substantial rise in gold production in the coming year.

"A significant further rise in attributable gold production can be expected in the coming year with a full year production from the Tanami Gold Mine," Otter said in a commentary accompanying its annual result.
The company reported net profit after tax of NZ$6.25 million, up from $1.21 million a year earlier.
Operating profit before tax and a legal damages award was up 110 percent at $4.97 million.
Net attributable gold production for the year was 53,093 ounces, up from 21,886 ounces produced in 1994/95.

Sale of gold and silver from mining operations resulted in revenue of $27.39 million, up 65 percent, largely as a result of the successful commissioning of the Tanami mine north-west of Alice Springs in Australia.
The net profit after tax included $3.58 million received as a damages settlement (net of legal costs) from a claim relating to pre-emptive rights under the Martha Hill joint venture.
Otter incurred tax of $1.92 million and said it expected $1.62 million of this to be deferred, with $0.3 million payable in respect of 1995-96.
At June 30 the group had cash resources of $8.1 million, and $12.5 million of undrawn funds under its finance facility with AIDC Ltd. $5.25 million was outstanding under the facility at year end.
